title: Supply & Construction
headline_read: Housing supply is out of balance — inventory or construction is strained.

indicators.title: Months of New-Home Supply
indicators.context: How many months it would take to sell every new home on the market at the current sales pace. Roughly 4-6 months is balanced; more is a glut, less is a squeeze.
indicators.read: 9.4 months of new-home supply — a glut that pressures prices and builders.

indicators.title: Active Listings (Realtor.com) · millions
indicators.context: Homes listed for sale nationwide, in millions (Realtor.com count, since 2016) — the inventory buyers actually get to choose from.
indicators.read: The number of homes for sale is little changed from a year ago, now 1.06 million.

indicators.title: Housing Starts · thousands, annual rate
indicators.context: New homes started each month, in thousands of units at an annual rate (1,465 means ~1.47 million homes/year) — the construction industry's output, and a classic leading indicator.
indicators.read: Homebuilding: down 9% from a year ago.

indicators.title: Building Permits · thousands, annual rate
indicators.context: Permits pulled for new housing units, in thousands at an annual rate — the step before starts, so it leads the rest of the construction pipeline.
indicators.read: Permitting: little changed from a year ago (-0%).
